text.p: Leading Estonian bank Hansapank on Tuesday said that it has increased its profit forecast for its bank activities to 380 million kroons and to 475 million kroons for Hansapank group.
The bank's original forecast was a profit of 256 million kroons and its original group 1997 forecast was 320 million kroons.
Hansapank, in a statement, also made a forecast of 11.3 billion kroons for its assets for 1997 and of 14.4 billion kroons for its group assets.
This compared with original forecasts of 7.8 billion kroons in assets for its bank and 9.594 for the group.

"Due to the faster than expected growth of the Estonian economy, the local banking sector and the whole Hansapank group during the first six months of 1997, Hansapank's board of directors revised the original forecasts made for 1997," the bank said in a statement.

Hansapank said the new forecasts were based on the assumption that the total assets of the bank sector would be 38.3 billion kroons by the end of the year and that its market share would 29.5 percent by the end of 1997.
It was also taking into account an expectation for a stable decrease in the productivity of its interest-earning assets.
